standard_prerequisites.name: A quotient of a regular local ring by an element is regular if and only if the element does not lie in the square of the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-regular-ring-CM}, cited at proof lines 11810-11812
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the local criterion verified by the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Leibniz rule for derivations
standard_prerequisites.use: Forces the derivative into the maximal ideal if the element lies in its square.

core_obligations: Reduce to a local regular ring with maximal ideal and residue field (proof lines 11808-11809).
Recall the criterion that the quotient is regular exactly when the element is not in the square of the maximal ideal (proof lines 11810-11812).
Rule out the bad case by the Leibniz rule (proof lines 11812-11814).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the local case (proof lines 11808-11809).
Leibniz rule excludes the bad case (proof lines 11812-11814).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a Jacobian criterion for hypersurfaces: if a regular ring admits a derivation sending an element to a unit of the quotient by that element, then the quotient is regular. The statement carries a slogan naming the criterion. The proof reduces to the local case with maximal ideal and residue field, where regularity of the quotient is equivalent to the element not lying in the square of the maximal ideal; were it to lie there, the Leibniz rule would force its derivative into the maximal ideal, contradicting the hypothesis.
